timeline.message:
Fix disabling `allow_leading_wildcard`

Disabling the `query_string` queries `allow_leading_wildcard` parameter didn't
work after a change probably introduced in #60959 because the various field types
`wildcardQuery` don't check the leading characters like
QueryParserBase#getWildcardQuery does. This PR adds the missing check also
before calling the field types wildcard generating method.

Closes #62267
timeline.author: Christoph Büscher

timeline.body:
Disabling the `query_string` queries `allow_leading_wildcard` parameter didn't
work after a change probably introduced in #60959 because the various field types
`wildcardQuery` don't check the leading characters like
QueryParserBase#getWildcardQuery does. This PR adds the missing check also
before calling the field types wildcard generating method.

Closes #62267
@markharwood would you mind taking a look since this small regression seems to be connected with one of your recent changes?
We should add the same check for prefix query too ?

reply.body: I'm confused how leading wildcard characters can start a prefix query. Wouldn't that only be "*" and "?", and wouldn't those get resolved as wildcard expressions?

I was confused because the QueryParserBase does the check on prefix query too (`field:*`) but we intercept these queries in ES to transform them into an exists query so there's no issue here. Sorry for the confusion.

timeline.body: I left one comment, LGTM otherwise

Sorry, only just got to looking at this.
The fix looks good but I wonder if a future consideration is if the flag is too blunt a tool?
While an admin may want to prevent expensive requests it's the combo of field and query that make something expensive, not query type alone. A `wildcard` field or low-cardinality `keyword` field could cope with leading wildcards fine. Is there more work to be done in scoping this flag?

> A `wildcard` field or low-cardinality `keyword` field could cope with leading wildcards fine. Is there more work to be done in scoping this flag?

Sounds like an interesting discussion in another issue. To me, in this case disallowing leading wildcards is a way to prevent "bad" user behaviour like leading wildcards in search boxes to take down or slow down clusters. `query_string` tends to get used when user input is passed down to ES unfiltered, which in itself is a questionable practice, but common. I think in this case having a "blunt tool" is desirable since the fields that are queries etc... are usually hard to control, but other cases might exist where this is different. Just my 20c.
